This is last because the discrepancy is 'unexplained, measured only' \u2014 it is an observation, not a confirmed guard death, and its blast radius is observability rather than correctness.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the three pre-v6 roots produce genuinely different verdicts by design (ERROR is the correct verdict for them), the discrepancy is not a defect and needs documentation, not a test.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the census delta is caused by a bug in the sweep instrument rather than verify_root_report, the test should target the instrument instead.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The census delta means the sweep instrument reports 11 ERRORs while direct-load reports 14 raising manifests \u2014 three roots surface as verdicts through verify_root_report rather than errors. This is an instrument-vs-instrument discrepancy, not a guard death. Blast radius: if the discrepancy indicates a real bug, verify_root_report may be silently swallowing three errors and presenting them as verdicts, hiding failures from operators. But because this is 'measured only' and 'unexplained,' it is the lowest-confidence gap. The cheapest test: run verify_root_report on the three pre-v6 roots and assert the output type (ERROR vs verdict) matches the documented expectation, forcing the discrepancy to be either fixed or explicitly documented as intentional.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
